findings.title: Uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: The newly added refresh block calls prisma.credential.update at line 96, but this file has no prisma import (imports are jsforce, RRule, zod, CalEventParser, constants, HttpError, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug and parseRefreshTokenResponse). This is a ReferenceError/TypeScript compile error and, if it compiled, would crash every Salesforce client construction at runtime.

findings.title: Fabricates dummy refresh_token and strips real token fields when sharing is enabled
findings.body: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is set, minimumTokenResponseSchema is a plain z.object, so Zod strips all fields except access_token (its computed keys are z.string().toString(), i.e. nonsense keys that do not allow other properties). Lines 25-27 then invent refresh_token='refresh_token'. Callers such as Zoom (key.refresh_token=newTokens.refresh_token; key.expiry_date=Date.now()+newTokens.expires_in*1000) therefore persist a fake refresh token and compute expiry_date as NaN, and Office365/Google lose expires_in/expiry, scope and token_type, permanently corrupting the stored credential so the next refresh fails.

findings.title: Stores SafeParse wrapper object as the credential key
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParse result {success,data}, not the parsed data. Previously this line used googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials) which returns the credential object itself. Now prisma.credential.update stores {success:true,data:{access_token,refresh_token}} as key. On the next use googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at line 75 will fail/misread because the stored key has the wrong shape, breaking the Google credential after the first refresh even when credential sharing is disabled.

findings.title: Returns raw fetch Response to callers expecting SDK/axios objects
findings.body: When sync is enabled this returns the raw fetch Response, but callers were written for incompatible return types: HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object (hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn/accessToken in hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192,202), ZohoCRM and Zoho Bigin expect an axios response with tokenInfo.data (zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217, zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96), and Google expects res.data (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-96, a fetch Response has no .data and needs .json()). Enabling sync therefore yields undefined tokens/expiry or TypeErrors for those integrations instead of refreshed tokens. No response.ok check or JSON parsing is done here either.

findings.title: Passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId) sends its third argument as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and only enables sync when it is truthy as a user id. This call passes credentialId (the credential primary key, captured at line 53) rather than credential.userId, which is not even retained in biginAuth. The parent application will be asked to refresh tokens for the wrong/nonexistent user.

findings.title: New Salesforce refresh discards refreshed token and corrupts stored key
findings.body: getClient now unconditionally refreshes on every construction, parses with parseRefreshTokenResponse, then at lines 96-99 overwrites the stored key with only {...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token} — in sharing mode the minimum schema strips id, issued_at, instance_url, signature, scope and token_type required by salesforceTokenSchema/future use. It then constructs the jsforce Connection at lines 101-108 with the old credentialKey.access_token/refresh_token, not the refreshed token, so the refresh has no effect apart from corrupting the DB row.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared non-constantly and header name not normalized; malformed input causes unhandled 500s
findings.body: The secret is compared with !== against req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret']; Node lower-cases incoming header names, so a configured value with any uppercase letter (the code does not toLowerCase it) will always reject legitimate calls, and the plain string comparison is timing-unsafe for a credential-writing endpoint. Separately, z.parse at line 31 and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) at lines 57-59 are uncaught, so an invalid body or undecryptable keys payload throws and returns an unhandled 500/stack behaviour instead of a 400, and there is no HTTP-method check.
